note: From the 2026-08-16 register-first verify pass (STVK gpo_bot_t layer). 7 trees verified and delivered to data/research/vilnius-verified.json. Leads failed only the evidence bar, the count, or ran out of the pass's time window; blocked can never ship as they stand. Register source for all: data/registers/lithuania-stvk-gpo.json.

leads.name: The oldest linden
leads.why: Named exactly like the oldest oak (vln_001) and 2.2km away, so a promising individually-named old tree. Not researched this pass: ran out of time budget before reaching it. Worth a dedicated search next pass (same Lithuanian-Wikipedia-stub pattern that worked for the university courtyard trees is likely to exist).

leads.name: Zverynas six-trunked linden
leads.why: Flagged in the brief as one of the most promising individually-named multi-stemmed trees. Forms a small second cluster with the Zverynas English oak (2.7km from centre, in the Žvėrynas neighbourhood). Not researched this pass, ran out of time; a second Vilnius walk (Žvėrynas) is plausible if both verify.

leads.name: Zverynas english oak
leads.why: Pairs with the Zverynas six-trunked linden above, 350m apart in the same neighbourhood. Not researched this pass; note the Lithuanian name literally means "narrow-branched oak" which may indicate a distinctive growth form worth checking, not necessarily the species Quercus robur x Q. petraea hybrid or an English/pedunculate cultivar; verify the species reading before writing.

leads.name: Castle park chestnut circle
leads.why: An ensemble candidate (a circle of chestnuts) similar in shape to the Vileisis palace maple circle below; both might pass the compact-famous-ensemble test but neither was researched this pass. Judge for photogenic compactness and a single obvious standing point before shipping.

leads.name: Maple circle in the P.Vileisis palace courtyard
leads.name_lt: P. Vileišio rūmų kiemo Klevų ratas
leads.why: Ensemble candidate, 1.8km from centre, in the courtyard of a historic palace (now home to the Lithuanian Theatre, Music and Cinema Museum). Not researched; worth checking whether the courtyard is genuinely open to the public before shipping (hard rule 10 access test).

leads.name: Presidential park oaks
leads.why: A group of oaks (plural) in the grounds around the Presidential Palace. Not researched: access needs checking (palace grounds vs. the adjoining public square) and it is a group name rather than a single named individual, so it needs the ensemble test applied.

leads.name: Bernardinai garden oak group / Group of four oaks in Sereikiškės park
leads.name_lt: Bernardinų sodo ąžuolų grupė / Keturių ąžuolų grupė Sereikiškių parke
leads.why: Named consistently in both the register and the general Bernardinų sodas Wikipedia article as a designated group of four oaks, so existence is corroborated by two sources, but no individual description was found to judge whether it reads as a single compact standing-point or as loose scattered oaks. In the same Bernardinai Garden cluster as the four already-shipped trees (vln_001, vln_005, vln_006, vln_007); worth a quick on-ground or satellite check next pass rather than shipping on a guess.

leads.name: Bernardinai garden ash (possible twin of the shipped three-trunked ash)
leads.why: Sits about 30m from vln_007 (the three-trunked ash already shipped). Could be the same tree double-registered, a genuine second ash, or the tree that Wikipedia's generic "Sereikiškių parko uosis" entry refers to. Register-pitfall twins should fold into one entry; needs a ground check or a clearer source before deciding whether this is a separate tree worth its own page.

leads.name: Birch of philologists
leads.why: In the same Old Town university courtyard cluster as the three shipped trees (vln_002-004), same register pattern (protected since 1996). Only one source found this pass (the register itself); a focused search did not surface a second independent source or a dedicated Wikipedia stub, unlike its neighbours. Worth another search pass, ideally in Lithuanian directly on a university or heritage site rather than general web search.

leads.name: Chestnut on Šiltadaržio street
leads.why: A single named individual chestnut, close to the Old Town / Bernardinai cluster. Not researched this pass for lack of time.

leads.name: Ash in Rose Alley
leads.why: A single named individual ash, 0.5km from centre. Not researched this pass for lack of time.

leads.name: Kalnai park pine
leads.why: Individual named pine, 1.3km from centre in Kalnai (Hill) Park, which has views over the Old Town. Not researched this pass.

leads.name: Swiss pine
leads.why: An individual named conifer, 2km out. Not researched this pass; "Swiss pine" (Pinus cembra) would be an unusual planted specimen in Lithuania and worth confirming the species carefully rather than assuming.

leads.name: Belunai Oak
leads.why: 9.8km out, inside the day-trip boundary if public transport reaches it within roughly 30 minutes (unverified). Not researched this pass.

leads.name: Canadian poplar in Castle park
leads.why: A single named individual poplar in the Castle park area. Not researched this pass; a Canadian poplar (introduced, fast-growing, relatively short-lived) is a weaker remarkable-tree case than the named oaks, lindens and multi-trunk specimens already shipped or listed nearby, so it is deprioritised rather than blocked.

leads.name: Pilaite Manor Pine
leads.why: 5.7km out, within Vilnius's own Pilaite district (reachable by city bus, so plausibly inside the day-trip boundary). Not researched this pass.

leads.name: Dirkliskes Forest Oak
leads.why: 13.7km out, likely beyond the 30-minute public transport day-trip boundary; would need a transit-time check before it could be presented honestly as part of a Vilnius page. Not researched this pass.

leads.name: Viktoras Bergas oak
leads.why: 17.4km out, almost certainly beyond the day-trip boundary. Not researched this pass; deprioritise below the closer candidates.

blocked.name: Vingis park linden alley
blocked.reason: An avenue, not a single collectible point. Matches the explicit hard-limit example ("An avenue or a whole wood is blocked"). Never ships as an entry, however notable the alley.

blocked.name: Old trees ("Senmedžiai")
blocked.reason: The register name is a generic Lithuanian word for "old trees" with no individual identity and no distinguishing description found. Not a collectible point as it stands; would need a source naming what specifically is there before it could even become a lead.

blocked.name: A group of Norway Maple in Cathedral Square
blocked.reason: Loose group of ordinary street/square maples on the edge of a large public square, not researched further because it reads as ordinary plaza planting rather than a famous, compact, one-obvious-place-to-stand ensemble (the La Rambla test). Would need a specific source arguing otherwise to reconsider.

blocked.name: A group of trees in Cathedral Square
blocked.reason: Same reasoning as the maple group above: a generic "group of trees" name on a large public square, no distinguishing description found, fails the collectible-point test as it stands.

blocked.name: Castle park tree group
blocked.reason: Generic "tree group" name, no distinguishing description found this pass; fails the collectible-point test as it stands. Could be revisited if a source describes it as a specific, compact, visually distinct planting.

blocked.name: Castle park linden group
blocked.reason: Generic "linden group" name, no distinguishing description found this pass; fails the collectible-point test as it stands.
